utterances.text: Was it necessary during the time period you were in Srebrenica to mobilise forces because of the war situation?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only time that I can remember is approximately midway through my stay there. The Muslims suffered a serious defeat to the south of Srebrenica, and they were very concerned about being overrun by the Serb forces. And I remember a -- the siren going off, and I was informed it was to mobilise the local fighters to deal with the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask that Lieutenant Colonel Dudley be shown P20, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: While that is being done, were you in a position distinguish between siren being an air-raid warning and siren being a call-up for fighters to gather?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would ask you to look at the paper in front of you. I believe the B/C/S will also be provided to you. And the document dated the 24th of March, 1993: "The commander of the Srebrenica armed forces hereby issues authorisation. The Kutlici unit is hereby authorised to mobilise the entire population temporarily housed in Kutlici village and send it to positions. Any person who refuses to obey the order of mobilisation shall be taken into custody at the prison in Srebrenica." It says that this same unit is "hereby authorised to confiscate and retain for themselves weapons from all those in possession of them who pass through or stay in Kutlici without a special pass stamped by the Srebrenica Armed Forces Staff." And then there's a name and a signature. My question to you, sir, is: Mobilisation of the entire population of Srebrenica is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let her finish the question first, because I haven't heard the entire question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's not what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Let me rephrase. Mobilisation of the entire population of Kutlici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Kutlici village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kutlici village, all right. And then, as it continues to go on to say of taking weapons or taking people into custody. Would that be in keeping with the dire situation that you found Srebrenica enclave in when you came?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will rephrase that question. Based on what I saw, there was a big difference between intent and capability. This document indicates intent. However, I doubt the forces on the ground had the capability of effectively carrying out that order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thank you very much for your response, but my question was: Is this document then in keeping from your experience in Srebrenica with the dire situation that the enclave was in?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: All this document tells me is that they're mobilising a village. I have no idea of -- and the population is temporarily in that village. So I have no idea of the size of this village and the amount of force sent to mobilise this village. So I cannot answer your question without some more information about the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. Can we say that from your experience in Srebrenica that certainly the ability to have weapons was very important to the Bosniak -- the Bosnian Muslims who were fighting in the enclave at that time period?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, because at this time they had been cut off. They had also suffered several local defeats. And their ammunitions situation particularly was abysmal. Another key problem that the forces inside Srebrenica had is that they did not have standardised weapons, therefore they could not share ammunition between different weapons. They would have to deal with -- you know, get new weapons when another weapon ran out of ammunition. We're dealing with hunting rifles and other non-standard equipment. So ammunition and weapons would go hand in hand. And therefore, to replenish their supply of arms, grabbing it from civilians or retrieving people who would possibly have them, would be a viable military option at this stage in the game.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I believe that you also testified that one of your watchers or assistants related to you a time period of when a person -- I believe it was a military person had been arrested and put in jail.

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First off I saw no mass arrests. There was only one time that it was mentioned to me that one person had been incarcerated in the jail, and that was a young man who had committed some type of a crime. What that crime is, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I would now ask if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And also yesterday he mentioned that it was a Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And without any submissions, I'm just going to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher now could that document be removed from Lieutenant Colonel Dudley, and I would now like to have document P178 placed in front of him, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Lieutenant Colonel Dudley, you've testified about the various front lines or defensive lines. And you've also testified how those lines were moving, in essence, shrinking, from a larger perimeter to a smaller perimeter by the time that you arrived. I would ask you to look at the document in front of you that's dated Srebrenica, the 15th of October, 1992, and it's an order. It says: "The free territory shall be secured by the established line of fire as follows." And I would ask you to look through the established lines of fire, and in particular line number 6 that says: "Likari, Caus, Djogazi, Budak, Pale, Bljeceva." Do you see where I'm referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, that goes on to say that these lines shall be secured and held by the Gornji Potocari Brigade, Gostilj Battalion, and Pale Battalion." My question to you is that during your time period in Srebrenica, were you aware of any front lines or line of fire established in those areas?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with these specific towns, except for the Potocari area, which I see is very close to the Drina River and Serbia. So I would need you to trace that on the map, that front line trace for me, and I can give you an honest yes or no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I believe you do have the map right next to you.

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I would direct your attention to Srebrenica. And I would ask you to look a little bit to the north and to the west, in like a semicircle around that area. I believe almost to the north where your pen was before I think we see the marking of Potocari. Yes. And so in those parameters I would ask you, were you familiar in your time period with any of the lines near Potocari, Likari, or Caus in its --

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can verify one specific line of confrontation because at the bridge at Potocari there was a Serb dug-in position on both sides of that road, and that's approximately where we did the prisoner exchange on the 21st. And -- so that part of the front line trace I can definitely confirm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then in keeping with your evidence concerning command and communications, intelligence, posting, stationing people on front line positions, would that be something that a commander or command structure should do, such as is evidenced in this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are now --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I tried to tie it in to his knowledge, particularly his knowledge of a certain line of defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have an acknowledgment from the witness already, acceptance on his part, that at least as far as Potocari or that area is concerned, there was a front line. Basically, it means that there was a front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I will leave it there, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So why --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I will leave it there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why proceed? Because we would have to go through the entire map and then ask him whether this was what was happening, and of course Caus on the mountain and all that, when he has already told you that they were, in his opinion, capable of mounting two assaults or attacks at the same time, simultaneously. So they barely had the people to do two things at the time. Did they have the people to man all these front lines? I don't know. If you want to ask him, of course by all means, but you need to keep your feet on the ground all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, they're right on the front lines, believe you me. My feet, I mean. And that's why I was just merely asking the witness if he was familiar with that one line, and I believe that he has answered in the affirmative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has told you yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He said Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Likari, Caus, Djogazi, Budak, Pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, we can remove the document from the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Dudley, I'd like to move now into a continuation but a slightly different area of the cross-examination, and I would like to show a video. And I believe this is exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you allow me just one second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It would be P427.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to the screen, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: If we could just go back a couple places, please. And then go forward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to ask you, if you look in the lower right-hand corner of this scene, are you familiar with what type of instrument or -- it looks like a satellite dish or a communications dish that's there?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't focussing on that when I was looking at the video, but from what I can see, it's a large white -- it looks like a dish with some type of antenna probe sticking out of the middle.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, we'll continue just a tiny bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in looking at it now, can you --

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an antenna dish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what type of capacity for communication that a disk like that could have, if you know, sir.

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we go back very slowly. I'd like to see what's behind it also, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. First I didn't see --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perfect. Okay. I haven't seen it communicate, therefore I don't know if it can communicate. It's always set up and looks like it's part of the UN capability, but if it has line of sight with another hilltop transmission site, it could probably be a long-range communicator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, was this your communication device or are we talking about a completely different type of communication device?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a totally different type of communication device. This was not mine. This is not man-packable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We're going to continue with this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I draw your attention to the person who appears to be using a phone apparatus. Now, is that phone apparatus in any way linked to that -- the use of the satellite dish you described?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: You always have to use some type of microphone or telephone in order to be able to communicate. I can't tell from this picture whether it's linked to the satellite dish or to the truck which is right next door to it. I would have to make the assumption, looking at which hand he's holding it in that it's linked to the truck itself. Probably it's HF communications, which was what normally the UN operated with. Again, I would like to say that UN and UNPROFOR did not have secure communications in the field when I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it from what you're saying, sir, that it's possible these are two different systems of communication that we're looking at now; one from the apparent phone-like instrument and the other from the satellite instrument.

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roger. And I cannot tell who is communicating using what device. I see a handset in the blue hat's hands, but I can't tell where it's going to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could we continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you just saw a person sling something over their shoulder. Were you able to discern what that might be?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It looked like a small portable backpack maybe for carrying water. So could I see it one more time? I'll look more carefully at it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It looked like a weapon. It looked like a collapsible AK automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll continue to go forward now, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the person who had the automatic weapon now appears to be speaking into an apparatus. I'm going to keep playing the video, and could you please tell us what type of apparatus that is.

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you right now. It's one of those Motorolas that they had inside Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are these the types of Motorolas that you saw while you were in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are referred to as bricks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you: Did you recognise anyone in the picture who was dressed in blue, with either a blue hat or a blue cap?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not recognise anybody who was associated with the UN section of UNPROFOR in that group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, when did UNPROFOR -- excuse me, sir. To your knowledge, when did personnel from UNPROFOR come into the area of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is two separate events that I'm aware of. The first one when General Morillon initially went into the Cerska pocket, which was just to the south -- excuse me, to the north of Srebrenica, trying to determine what was going on in that area. And there's a lot of activity associated with that. And then once he got permission, he -- a small group came in on the 11th of March, and that was part of that second group. So the first time we approached the Srebrenica area/pocket as an UNPROFOR group was at Cerska, entry by General Morillon, with a very small group of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are we speaking about March of that -- of 1993, sir?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the exact date on top of my head. I would say the end of February/beginning of March time frame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm sure the Prosecution doesn't want to have misleading evidence on this either, so I think it's important to clarify this. Are we talking about the whole period that the UN was ever in Srebrenica? Because, of course, this witness is just speaking about up to March 1993. But as we've seen, there's no time indication on this video. Is he being asked whether up until 1995 the UN was present? And I would also -- I would like to be clear whether the Prosecution is actually trying to suggest that the satellite dish was not belonging to the UN blue helmets there. There's only so much I can address in re-examination. If that's the suggestion, I think I need to know that so I can address that, because that seems to be almost the suggestion. And if so, then I think, in fairness to the witness and to get the best evidence, we should look carefully what the blue caps are, what's written on it, because otherwise there's a suggestion and insinuation but it's not actually being stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think this satellite dish ownership matter needs to be addressed, because obviously you have asked the witness whether he could enlighten us on what that could possibly be, and he said that's a satellite dish, depending on what for. So I think the Defence --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly. Let me clarify the two questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- need to know --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: -- was for this witness, when was the first time that he knew in his knowledge that United Nations personnel, UNPROFOR, came into Srebrenica. And we can certainly go to the second question, because I'm not attempting to suggest anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the satellite dish we saw on this video belonged to the United Nations or to anyone else in Srebrenica? If you know, tell us; if you don't know, state, "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you that we talked about communications and transportation. And while you were with your watchers or your assistants, did you at any time learn about the ability to take helicopters in and out of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had one report, and that was from Senad, that they were using a Gazelle helicopter from Tuzla to ferry in a few people and to ferry out a few wounded, and maybe to bring in a few supplies. But they could only do it at night, and very carefully, because they would be interdicted and shot down by the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when -- I'm sorry, sir. When you say that "they were using," could you be a bit more explicit, if you can.

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly: BiH forces inside Bosnia and Herzegovina, particularly between Tuzla and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were there any persons in Srebrenica, to your knowledge, that you were informed of who would ever take these helicopters and come -- go out of Srebrenica to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only person would be the -- was Naser was referred to as once having left the pocket that I can recall. Anybody else, I don't know. The only other person, I think, who possibly could have gotten in and out was Tony Birtley, but I don't -- I cannot confirm or deny that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like now to show the witness another videotape. If you would just allow me to speak to case manager.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll be looking at P517.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Dudley, I would ask you to look at this image that's in front of you now, and I would ask you, if you can, would you identify what type of weapon that is.

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. It is an assault automatic machine-gun, it looks like, with a drum canister. It would be part of the former Yugoslav JNA weapons inventory. I believe he's wearing a sling over his shoulder for support, which is not a good way of using that weapon because of the recoil. I would expect to see it with a bipod or a tripod in a fixed position so they could deliver accurate weapons fire with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know or can you tell whether, by the manner in which the person is dressed, whether that's a member of the armed forces of Republic of Srpska or from forces that would be from the ABiH forces or Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The picture is too blurry for me to see any distinguishing features in this one, so I'm not going to speculate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record -- one moment. For the record, the witness is looking at a still from the said video P517 at 03.46.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to look at the next video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to discern from this still picture here what type of weapons that are being shown?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same type I saw before, and again it looks like it has either a box or a round canister to hold the ammunition. And again, that keeps the weapon from jamming when fired. It is a light machine-gun of some sort. Again I would expect to see a bipod or a tripod with it. Obviously this is inside Srebrenica because I can see the building where we did the prisoner release just off to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to run this just a tiny bit so you can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just wanted to record the still, please, where the witness was making his comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, can we also remove the wording below because that's -- it doesn't seem to correspond and it's also practically inflammatory, I think, that appearing there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but are we going to ask the witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not looking at the wording.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If the witness could disregard as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are at still 05.28.04.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, I would ask that we just roll it a bit more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you've testified briefly that you were unable in many ways to meet the political and military leadership of Srebrenica. I'm going to ask you, did that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He didn't exactly say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He met the mayor, he met members of the War Presidency. The only person he didn't meet was Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: May I rephrase that, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to meet with various members of the military leadership, such as local commanders, such as commander -- staff commanders, or with any of their immediate subordinates?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer to that is: No. And that was one of my most difficult issues in Srebrenica. So I needed to liaison to do specific planning or find out what was going on with the tactical situation on the ground. I was not able to meet with many key players that I can remember or that I recorded. And therefore, it was initially difficult for me to figure out what was going on in that environment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And prior, maybe, to being pre-empted by Judge Agius, I just want to make it clear then that you therefore did not attend any meetings of military hierarchy while you were there?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to go back to my memory as best I can. There was an initial meeting the first night we were in Srebrenica in the PTT building, in a little conference room next to where they had the ham radio station. I don't remember being part of that meeting. Now, I might have sat in on that meeting, but I was very tired, I didn't record it, therefore I have no real recollection or memory of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in terms of other authorities, you met the mayor of the town, if I'm correct.

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I was later informed that that was the mayor I shook hands with, and I could definitely pick out his picture, and I remember him being addressed as something like that. I also met with a member of the War Presidency. I remember having dinner with him in his apartment one night while I was there. But I don't remember being able to have an opportunity to sit down and have many in-depth meetings with either the War Presidency personnel or, you know, their field commanders or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than those two persons, the mayor and the War Presidency, did you meet any other civilian authorities or leaders in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might have. However, I didn't record it and did not record on my brain as a key meeting or a key event during my time that I was there. And I would take that to mean that it didn't register as important enough for me to record or to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can I also take that to mean that you didn't have the opportunity, therefore, to discuss any military tactics with any military leaders nor any civilian matters that might come up with the civilian leaders?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not go into depth with any of them. One of the key remembrances I had was having dinner with that War Presidency individual is we beat around the bush a little bit, but I got nothing firm out of them. One of my key frustrations, again, is when I would try to carry on a conversation with a lot of these people, we would go around and around in circles, but nothing would be accomplished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But yet, you did know, even though you didn't meet with the person, that this Naser appeared to be the commander of the military. Is that correct, or am I misstating what you said?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will re-word your question. From everybody I talked to, they all said that Naser was the local commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to show another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, one moment. Do you still have a comment or a remark --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: There are various -- I'm not going to state what the witness has said before because it might be suggested that I am hinting at something. But if Ms. Sellers could -- if she's actually going to state what the witness said, if she could refer to the page and line so we can actually check that, then that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Sellers. We are approaching the end anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we are. I would now ask that the witness be shown video 4 -- I'm sorry. Video -- P number 427. And if we could just look at the screens, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Dudley, on the frame in front of you, and you see that there is -- appears to be a date of the 6th of March, 1993, and what appears to be a group of uniformed men and then some persons including children who are not in uniform. My first question to you is: Can you tell us what type of weapon appears to be carried by the person in the background?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Wait before you answer. We are at still 24.43.1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can we go back and play the video again, and I'll be looking for that specific part of the picture. Oh, perfect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop. Okay. That is a light assault machine-gun. It's got the same -- now I can see it better. It looks like the same one that I saw before, and it's a boxed ammunition carrier -- you can see the rounds feeding into the chamber. And you can see the tripod -- I mean the bipod up front. They can be folded down and used to provide support for the weapon on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, just a very quick side question. You've described now two or three times these light assault machine-guns. Are these are the types of weapons that you previously testified about that are easy to carry over rugged terrain and are more mobile compared to heavier types of artillery?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And you can see -- this picture is much clearer. I can point out some other military gear here that I recognise, too, from the past.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, yes.

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. You can see the sling over the man's shoulder. He's got one box of ammunition attached to the machine-gun, and I would assume that other members of his group would carry additional boxes of ammunition to support him, and usually you fire this weapon as part of a two-man team, one being the firer and the other one being the loader, who would make sure that the rounds fit evenly into the machine-gun for smooth firing. Also you see the Bandolier that the other gentleman has in the middle. That's very typical of North Korean/Chinese gear at the time and that's where he would carry his banana clips for his Kalashnikov assault rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is this similar to what you described -- I'm speaking to the man who seems to be standing a bit to the right-hand side of the screen who is in uniform, was this similar to the type of apparatus you were describing a uniform that Senad wore?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: This looks like Senad himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was going to be my next question.

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's got the green beret on. He's got the same exact vest on as the other gentleman, and he's wearing the same type of uniform that I had seen many times in the past on him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll let that roll a little more and you might be able to get a slightly clearer shot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was Senad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, so is this the person --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Ms. Sellers. We are now at 24.43.5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, when you say "Senad," this was the person who was your watcher/assistant?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the type of uniform that he's wearing, is that a type of uniform that was worn by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me clarify that, and I'm going to give you what he told me is his personal history. He claimed to be a Croatian Muslim who had grown up in Srebrenica. He had fought -- he volunteered to be part of the Green Berets, which was part of the initial attempt by the BiH to establish military organisations. He considered himself an elite fighter. He fought initially in Croatia and then had come to Tuzla, where he had volunteered to be part of a small group infiltrating into Srebrenica. I believe he brought the German photographer with him about the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you recognise any of the other uniforms that the other males appear to be wearing as uniforms that were worn by Muslim fighters, military combatants or --

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: This group seems to be a little bit better equipped than most of the ones that I saw, and it might be a little bit earlier in the environment, which means that they were in a little bit better shape. You notice that there's a wide variety of military uniforms within the group; it's not uniform. Looking at the man on the far left, you can see he is wearing one type of pants, camouflage pants, he's wearing another type of jacket. One guy looks like he has some type of head skull cap on, but again they are all in various motley types of uniform. But, yes, this would be typical fighters, plus any other cold-weather gear they could wear when I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Senad or any of the others you see here have any type of designation of a lily or something of the ABiH army?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have one patch that I have at home as a souvenir that actually showed the lily or the -- the BiH insignia. I have not seen it on these guys. I saw occasionally in Srebrenica, but very rarely. And I would just like to make a military note on that. If I were in a combat situation, that's one patch I would immediately cover over because it's too visible. It's not camouflage. It's bright yellow and blue, et cetera, which make it stand out, and that makes for a nice target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're going to continue this video for just a couple seconds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Dudley, I'd like to ask you, the men that you see in uniform in this portion of the video, are these also similar to some of the uniforms that you saw while in the enclave in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a few people in uniform like this, but most of them didn't have the gear. Most of them were village people who did not have full military uniforms. This individual directly in front of me is unusual because he looks very well-uniformed for the environment. He's got a heavy military coat on. He's got American-style web gear, it looks like. It looks like he's wearing some type of a patch over his right pocket -- excuse me, his left pocket. Some of the things that are very unmilitary, though, is that yellow or orange thing he has close to his neck. Again, that would make for a bad target. So although he looks relatively well-equipped, he doesn't look well trained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would advise him to take the yellow --

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would tell him to take the yellow off, I would tell him to take that patch off, and I would tell him that he looks like he might be rattling around a little bit too much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We're going to continue rolling this a little bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We were, for the record, at 25.20.3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Will you stop the tape, please. I would like to go back about four bars because I would like to make a comment here. Stop -- no, go back, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop. See this man with the multi-coloured hat on, ski hat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is more likely what I saw there. And they guy with his regular coat on, you've got a little bit more of a uniformed group here, but you have a lot of other guys who are a lot less uniformed, a lot less disciplined, and that's more like what I saw in Srebrenica, not this small group of relatively well-uniformed individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, given the climate in Srebrenica, that time period, would you say that the discipline, in terms of military discipline, would prohibit people wearing wool hats or things that would give them warmth in addition to their uniform?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: You do what you got to do in the environment in which you find yourself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll continue rolling this for just a --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, could you look at this weapon in front of us now and could you tell us what type of weapon that is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Wait, wait, wait. For the record, we are at 26.22.9.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, it's very blurry to me, but it looks like a form of sniper rifle. Let me point out some reasons why I think so. This looks -- I can't remember the exact name, but this is a very common weapon within the Warsaw Pact forces, and I'm going to say what I think. Okay? And if I could have a better military picture, I could confirm or deny what I'm going to say. You see it's got a wooden/hard plastic stock in the back. It's got a very large shoulder rest. It's got some type of telescopic scope. I can't see the large part of the barrel, but it's got a very large, heavy barrel, which looks like it would be firing a large-calibre bullet. And again it's got that tripod upon which you could get a steady hold and provide more stability for the weapon to snipe with. So I would call this a sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. We'll continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask now if we could just go into private session because there will be a part of this video that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't need to explain for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there an objection? No. So we are, for the record, still at 26.47.8. And let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I just need to confer with my colleagues for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What kind of re-examination do you have, Mr. Jones? How long do you think you will last?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think it will be about 40 minutes. There's a lot --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: 40, 4-0. There have been a lot of documents, a lot of videos, and I need to address each of them, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead. Please try to conclude, Ms. Sellers, as quickly as you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. We have an exhibit that the Defence has used on several occasions, and it's a book called "Merry Christmas, Mr. Larry." And I would like to see if the pages we have designated can be given to Lieutenant Colonel Dudley. Could we put it on the ELMO. I would ask that you put it on page 173.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would ask you to look at page 173, and please first just note -- I don't know whether you're familiar with the book or not, but to note the author of the book from the title page.

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Check.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you read the book before, sir?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not. Let me rephrase that, I have read a small portion of the book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you read the portion of the book where you were in it or other portions?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few other portions also. I think I have read this portion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 173, there at the top of the page it says: "Their commander is Naser Oric, a tough leader who rules with a rod of iron." And then further down on that page at the beginning of one of the paragraphs it says: "Naser Oric sent a vehicle to pick up the General. The rest of us struggled for hours, forcing a gap wide enough to let our vehicle pass." Now, you testified that you did not meet Naser Oric, did not know who Naser Oric is. Did you ever hear of a reputation of him being a strong person, someone who might rule with a rod of iron?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me answer as honestly as I can on this question. First off, I did not hear any personal reports on Naser that were not positive or complimentary to him. In the environment in which he was existing, any commander would have to apply what I would call tough love in that environment to keep his soldiers moving in the right direction. Sometimes you can pat them on the back, but more you have to lead by example and you have to have very strict discipline, or as much as you can, of course, to keep the people doing the right thing at the right place at the right time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, are you saying therefore, in a positive vein, that Naser Oric might have been someone who ruled with a rod of iron?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first off, he would have to have the respect of the people who were following him. If he lost that respect, then he would be an incompetent commander. So abusing his subordinate soldiers would not be a smart thing to do. However, enforcing good military discipline would be something he would have to do, and he would have to insist on it from the subordinate commanders as well in order to conduct small-unit dispersed type operations that were being conducted in the pocket while I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We can remove that exhibit from the witness. I'm going to my very last video --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This hasn't got a number as yet --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could I ask for a P number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will become Prosecution Exhibit P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 615. I thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I really hope we don't run out of time, but I've always been clear how much time I needed. And Ms. Sellers was going to finish at 1.00 and each video takes us -- if it's--

utterances.speaker: MR. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: -- five minutes, then we'll go into tomorrow, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the last video of five minutes and I think that it's a very -- it's important --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm making it clear, at this point in time I am not going to deprive Mr. Jones from the time that he has indicated he needs. I am not going to keep anyone here a minute beyond the time, because we have been here sitting since 8.00 in the morning and the reporter has been using her hands all the time since then. So we will have to stay here and continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand this video is three minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, prior to looking at this video, I would just like to ask you to recall your testimony concerning the day when you arrived in Srebrenica and that you described a type of blockage that, to your knowledge, was spontaneous in terms of people being kept in the PTT building. Will you just confirm that to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I would like to say is what I observed was a large crowd of mostly women, old men, children, broken up into family groups that were camped outside the PTT building. And they sort of converged on us when they found out who was there and what was going on. And there seemed to be a lot of mass hysteria. I didn't see any organised people floating around/making the crowd perform to their beat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, would you also confirm that, in your experience, a commander takes decisions and lays down conditions in very difficult situations?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a question, again, I'm going to have to give a lengthy answer to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We don't have the time. Is it possible --

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I will pass on the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly you can pass on the question. And my last question prior to just showing you this video is that you confirmed that to your knowledge there were no other authorities, no authorities, engaged in this holding of the persons inside the building at abeyance. I believe that was your testimony.

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it appeared to be a spontaneous crowd around the building. I didn't see any specific people putting a firm guard on us that I can recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of any conditions to stop the spontaneous crowd from ...

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the crowd seemed to be very insistent that General Morillon stay and not leave. That seemed to be the key condition for the crowd dispersing, and then we could start to do our job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, did you know on that day - and I think we're talking about the 11th of March - did you know that Naser Oric was the commander in the area?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I had no clue before going into the pocket and immediately upon arriving in the pocket who the actual commander was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you find out soon thereafter that he was the commander?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe on the second or the third day was when his name was initially mentioned to me as the commander on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll come back to this on re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to show the video, but I would like to hand up the translations of the transcript of this video. This is P427 again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Dudley, did you recognise anyone in that video?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously you're making me draw a conclusion that's Naser sitting up on the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm not, sir; I'm asking you do you recognise anyone in that?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. There were a couple, obviously, civilians. I heard a British voice. I don't know who that was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, again, it's the problem. There was a suggestion underneath with the words of who it was, but since the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I told you, I mean, the witness can perfectly handle each and every situation that has arisen. I'm not conceding, Mr. Jones, at any time you are trying to suggest anything to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my question, my final question, sir, is after looking at this video, I put it to you, would you change your mind that there might have been authorities also involved in this taking or this holding of people at abeyance in the PTT building on the 11th of March, when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to give you what I know and then I'm going to tell you what I think. What I know is that when we arrived there, there was a huge crowd of family groups that night. And obviously we still had some light when this was happening. Okay. So I don't think this happened that same night. I think that was happening the next day. Whenever you have a group like General Morillon come into a besieged town, I would expect local commanders and other authorities to show up because this is a key event, a very important event, to include the local military commander. He was probably putting out his demands, and he appears to be a very charismatic leader because the people are cheering him and agreeing with him and are very excited that he's come here to suffer with you, and all this other good stuff. But I don't think he was there that same night when we were initially blocked in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, sir, and I thank you for your testimony on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I thank you as well, Madam Sellers. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I observe that I was 2 and a half hours in examination-in-chief and the Prosecution has been 3 hours and 15 minutes, much longer than me. I always said I needed 45 minutes and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You will have all the 45 minutes that you need.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I do apologise to the witness and the US government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I know, Mr. Jones. I am not blaming you, at all, for what happened. But I said very clearly that if you need 40 minutes, you'll get 40 minutes. If you need 45, you'll have 45. There's no going back on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Re-examined by Mr. Jones:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Colonel, you have been asked today, or you've referred on more than one occasion to Naser as a local military commander you also said that there were "other military authorities." And in answer to my questions yesterday, you said that there were multiple players, military speaking. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could determine, there were multiple players on the ground, both civil and military. I have a personal request. Could we take a quick two-minute break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think we could afford to do that. We'll have a five-minute break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. --- Break taken at 1.22 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just for the transcript, I know it's being cleaned up afterwards, and I know it's my fault also for going too quickly, but I don't think your answer was fully reflected. I reminded you that you said that there were other military authorities and that there were multiple military players and I think you confirmed: Yes, there were multiple players on the ground, military and civilian. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your information was that Naser was among those military players. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will rephrase your question. Were there multiple individuals who were dealing with civil or military affairs in Srebrenica? That is correct. Naser seemed to be first among equals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, regarding any relationship between Senad and Naser, I don't want you to speculate or make any assumptions, I simply want to ask you a series of questions. Did Senad ever manage to arrange a meeting with Naser?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know for a fact, apart from what he told you, whether he ever spoke to Naser?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that he actually spoke to Naser at any time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever see him with Naser?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as Zele is concerned, did Zele ever mention Naser to you?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once or twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what language was that?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been in Serbo-Croatian, and it would have been translated by Senad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Senad speaking in a combination of German and English?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Senad dealt with other people as well, did he not, in Srebrenica, the War Presidency, the mayor, and other people?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. Actually, he was my translator whenever I was talking to anybody, and also I saw him interacting with lots of different people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, just in case you may need to refer to this video and its transcript later on, I'm referring to the last video shown by the Prosecution, and more particularly to the transcript thereof, the transcript does not have an exhibit number and I'm giving it one. And the transcript will now become Prosecution Exhibit P427.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Senad, you told us, arrived I think you said in February 1993. You told us today what he told you about raids and that sort of thing. So would it be correct that what he told you related to the period after he arrived in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, there's a discussion at various points today of terminology of units, groups, et cetera. As far as the term "brigades" is concerned, in your observations in Srebrenica, was that ever applied, in fact, to small units in a loose sense?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say all military terms, be it brigade, battalion, company, unit were very loosely used in this situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did the reality on the ground in fact reflect how one might understand those terms in a conventional sense?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not apply at all. We're talking about -- I'm going to use the term non-trained fighters who were basically giving themselves their own designations versus what was actually -- would be considered reality on the ground with a fully equipped, fully armed brigade or battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I don't want to rehearse your testimony yesterday about there being no or very few uniforms, about there being no signs of ranks, semi-autonomous village groups, asymmetric warfare, almost non-existent communications, no trained leaders. What I do want to ask you is in light of any of the questions or documents or videos you've been shown today, does that affect your conclusions at all in what you said yesterday on those matters?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing that has influenced just a little bit is that there was an attempt - and I want to use the term "attempt" - to get some organisation within their structure. But what they attempted and what they succeeded to do are two totally different things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So apart from that observation, do your conclusions and your observations remain the same?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they remain the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you referred yesterday -- you referred today to conducting small-unit raids and ambushes. Was there, in fact, any other way that the Muslims could fight the Serbs under those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the most effective way, based on what they had available to them at the time. I want to also add it appears that they tried to do some larger-scale military operations, and they failed at those attempts, probably suffering more casualties than they wanted to incur. And therefore, they fell back on to individual and small-unit type operations, which were much safer for them to conduct and required a lot less command and control requirements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And it was put to you that the terrain was an advantage for the Muslims being on foot. Did they have any advantages, apart from that, if that can be described as an advantage, vis-a-vis the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not have any other advantages. They were outgunned, outequipped, et cetera, by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as travelling on that terrain is concerned, you were there, you saw the terrain. It was suggested or stated that it was very easy for light infantry to infiltrate. How easy, in fact, would it be for a fighter to walk 20 or 30 kilometres in that terrain in heavy snow over mountains? Is that easy?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me rephrase that in two parts. One, if you know the terrain and you were trained in mountainous warfare, yes, and if you have the right equipment, be it snowshoes, et cetera. If you're not familiar with the terrain and you are not properly equipped and you aren't experienced in that type of an environment, no, it would be extremely difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which of those two scenarios was it in Srebrenica, from what you could observe?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it was a combination of both. We had a lot of local boys who were very familiar with the terrain and the trails, and therefore they would be able to get around relatively easily. But for civilians, particularly those who had been forced out of their home villages, they would have to stick to the main roads and the trails, because otherwise they would get lost and confused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it depends on how much familiarity, and that is a question of fact?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were also asked about whether it could be an advantage for a fighter to be living with his family because, in a way, he would be fiercer. Isn't it the case that also detracts from command and control because you can choose to stay at home rather than go to fight?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it can be both ways. If you're defending your home and your family against intruders and they're depending on you, that will make you very fierce because you're defending your own. However, if your family is in need just for food for basic survival, then you're torn in two directions; defending your environment from the enemy but also providing for your family. And that would make for major problems with command and control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked about a number of facets of military life, if you like, in Srebrenica. You said you preferred to use the word "combatant" military combatant rather than "soldier." Can you elaborate on that, why you prefer not to use the word "soldier."

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Soldier" means that he has received some type of training and that he is uniformed and equipped, however poorly, to be part of an organisation or unit. "Military combatant" means that they have grouped together for self-defence or for some type of military reaction, usually reacting to some type of invasion. They don't have the equipment, uniform equipment, and training to work as an effective fighting force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were asked about matters such as rotation on the front lines. Was there actually anything as formal as rotation, or was it simply that fighters can't stay on the lines forever and sooner or later they have to be replaced?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am going to, again, state what I observed. What I observed while I was there was that units had a semi-agreed method of rotating on to and off the front lines. Please remember, this was March, it was cold, particularly when they were out at night, and staying out for more than 24 hours at a time would be very rigorous if you didn't have the right winter equipment to survive in that environment. These people did not, to my observation, so staying out for more than 24 hours at a time would have been difficult. Therefore, they sort of rotated in and out, with a gentlemen's agreement, every 24 to 48 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A gentlemen's agreement means something not binding, correct?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But let me rephrase that: Not binding but you have a loyalty to your buddy. He's going to do it for you, you're going to do it for him. It was more that close cohesiveness after years of warfare that convinced them to support each other out of mutual loyalty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you about Motorolas and I want to remind you what you said yesterday about that. It was page 66, lines 19 to 22, for our reference, and you were talking the PTT building. You said: "In that same room where I mentioned the ham radio operators, or in the adjacent room, I can't quite remember which, they had torn-apart Motorola radios that they were trying to piece together to form at least one functional set." Now, did you actually see functional Motorolas when you were in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not -- wait, let me take that back. I think there was one instance where I saw a functional Motorola and that was the day that we were doing the air evacuation of the wounded. I believe the police had one in Srebrenica and another one down at the soccer field to confirm that they had secured the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So apart from that, apart from that one or two that you saw, you didn't see any other functioning Motorolas?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I did not see them in active use and there didn't appear to be a lot of them. Let me further elaborate: They didn't have the electricity, except in the PTT building, to provide a charging unit for these Motorolas, and therefore it was very difficult to keep them charged, and also they didn't have repair parts for them. So when they broke, that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And RUPs, did you see any functional RUPs?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see functional groups --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: RUPs, R-U-P. You were asked about RUPs. Firstly, is that something different from a Motorola? You were asked about RUPs.

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the definition of RUP, you would have to explain that acronym to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, it was something you were asked about, and aside from the Motorolas, did you see any other hand-held device?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you aware of any repeaters in the Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked about couriers. Now, when you speak of couriers, is that anything different from simply people running back and forth? Is there actually anything you're referring to which is different from that, people taking messages on foot?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: A courier in this environment would have at least had some experience with the terrain and the group he was working with and the key leaders he would be delivering the messages to. So in that case I would call him a semi-trained individual who knew a specific job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. I want to be clear about terminology versus what you observed. Did you actually observe trained couriers taking messages back and forth? Is that something you saw with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think, in fact, in speaking on the subject, you referred to earlier centuries, as a system which was used in earlier centuries. Is people running back and forth with messages, is that a primitive or a sophisticated form of communication?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the earliest form of communication in early warfare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were shown -- I don't think I need to necessarily put it on the screen -- P446. It was a video, and you were asked about a typewriter, whether you saw a typewriter. First of all, were you able to see from that film when it was filmed or where it was filmed, or anything of that nature at all?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to state that it looked like it was early time in Srebrenica, looking at the condition of the people sitting around the table. And --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I stop you there. You might to see the video again, because I would like to ask you why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If I remember well, it does have a date.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, there is a date on the screen. It doesn't necessarily --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, but I ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you say it was Srebrenica rather than Tuzla, Mostar, or any other of a dozen different locations?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't claim that just from the location inside that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I was asking. Were you able to tell from that whether the typewriter was operating; whether it had a ribbon, for example?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I could not tell that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were also directed to note that there was a pile of papers and a pen. If you saw -- if you saw some papers and a pen, would you conclude from that that all the conditions for C3I exist, that there's command and control?

utterances.speaker: REX EDWARD DUDLEY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I'll stop there, in fact, because I come to the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Lieutenant Colonel, we'll need to stop here. We've had a long session, long sitting. We'll finish with you very quickly tomorrow morning first thing. I do apologise to you for having you brought back again tomorrow, and as well as to the representatives of the US government. I do apologise to you, but I think we don't have any option. I should like to thank the reporter in particular. I know how hard it is to do that job for almost -- I don't know how many hours, I lost count now. Thank you so much. Thanks to the technicians and interpreters and the rest of the staff. We'll meet again tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of December, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.44 p.m.,
